{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZkdeaw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDLEHQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 123, "title": "Add evidence-qualified scheduled delivery of local resident mail", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `1bc9ab05750a63b2f506ae1ba12bbdd8eea08266`, mail composition saves ordinary letters immediately. There is no pending-delivery state, date/time selection, pending inspection or cancellation journey. This is an existing historical-fidelity omission, not a demonstrated regression from PR #122.

## Expected outcome

Enable this terminal journey from MAIN `1`, MAIN `X` and DAISIZEN `MAIL`:

`WRITE-AT resident → select future simulated-JST date/time → compose → review/edit → approve → inspect pending letter → reload/restore → cancel before due or release once when due → SENT/READ`

Use intentionally reconstructed commands: `WRITE-AT address`, `PENDING`, `READ-PENDING reference` and `CANCEL-PENDING reference`. These names are product controls, not recovered historical syntax. Restrict this increment to a new plain-text letter from the selected human to one existing local resident.

Pending letters must remain outside delivered correspondence and resident knowledge. Deterministic local delivery must work with AI disabled or unconfigured. Resident responses remain optional and subject to existing consent, timing and generation limits.

## Context

### Historical evidence and accepted reconstruction

Sources inspected live on 2026-10-24:

- [NEC PC-VAN office account, March 1993, printed p. 231](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jkg/43/3/43_KJ00002959297/_pdf/-char/ja) explicitly documents delivery at a specified date and time. Confidence is high within that earlier period. The [publisher record](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jkg/43/3/43_KJ00002959297/_article/-char/ja/) confirms NEC affiliation and publication on March 1, 1993. PDF text was readable with damaged OCR spacing; page-image retrieval failed.
- [Internet Magazine, November 1996, printed p. 221](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199611-220-mail2.pdf) documents PC-VAN Internet-mail sending/reception and `INET#` addressing. It supports preserving the separate external-mail journey, but supplies no scheduled local-mail controls.

Focused searches using 日時指定, 予約メール, 予約送信, 送信予約 and 配達指定 recovered no qualifying late-1996 scheduling sequence. ECOM postal-service excerpts were excluded from ordinary electronic-mail requirements. Failed page-image retrieval did not prevent inspection of readable publisher metadata and the separate contemporary magazine source.

**Accepted category D reconstruction:** continued availability in late 1996 is a moderate-confidence continuity inference. Commands, prompts, pending references, review geometry, cancellation rules and local scheduling limits are authored choices. Accept minute-resolution input, a future horizon of at most 30 elapsed days, and browser-resume reconciliation. These are application limits, not historical claims. Existing shared current/old/SIG mailbox projections remain qualified reconstructions.

Nothing runs while the browser is closed. An overdue letter is processed on the next active visit. Preserve the intended delivery instant separately from actual persistence/processing time, and document how retrospective catch-up uses that availability instant. Do not fabricate historical delivery by merely changing `createdAt`.

Historical cancellation procedures, scheduling limits, original timezone presentation and mailbox-transition relationships remain unresolved. These uncertainties do not block this disclosed subset. Attachments, scheduled replies, multiple scheduled recipients, external scheduled delivery and mailbox migration are outside scope.

### Implementation and duplication evidence

The checkout matches the baseline and has a clean worktree.

- `src/commands.ts:startCompose`, `recordsHistory` and `invalidate()` provide recipient pinning, registration, input ownership and stale-draft handling.
- `src/composer.ts` provides literal multiline text, review, editing, cancellation, explicit approval and consumed-commit behavior.
- `src/storage/repository.ts:createHumanMail`, `createHumanMultiMail`, `insertMail` and `transaction` provide transactional writes, monotonic delivered-mail numbering and world-generation fences.
- `src/storage/schema.ts` strictly validates Mail fields and relationships; it currently has no scheduled-mail representation. Existing validated reserved settings provide a persistence precedent without requiring another database subsystem.
- `src/calendar.ts` projects operational instants through a durable historical anchor. Scheduling needs an explicit inverse of that mapping, independent of browser timezone.
- `src/ai/mail.ts:chooseMail`, `pairMail`, `src/ai/activity-runner.ts` and `commitAiRun` determine recipient context and catch-up chronology. Existing runner filtering uses `simulation.simulatedAt ?? createdAt`; scheduled availability must be handled consistently wherever relevant.
- `src/main.ts` already has startup, focus/resume, content refresh and visible-minute activity boundaries suitable for reconciliation.

Live repository queries returned no open Issues or PRs. Exact scheduled-delivery history search recovered [#119](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/119), which explicitly deferred this capability; 日時指定 search returned no matches. Existing tests mentioning “scheduled mail” concern autonomous resident visits, not sender-selected delivery times.

[PR #122](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/122) and `docs/validation.md` report 25 focused OSL checks, 29 affected composer checks and a final complete run of 480 passing checks with three workers, including configured type checking/build. They record a corrected stale-composer failure. These are Coordinator records, not checks run by this research graph; previous timing/default-worker reliability questions remain unresolved.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Make scheduling and pending inspection discoverable across all three mail entry routes, preserving their contextual returns. Reuse existing human registration and resident-address resolution. Reject external, human, unknown and ambiguous destinations. Pin the resident ID and safe display label; renaming cannot retarget a draft.
- [ ] Collect `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` in the shared simulated JST calendar, showing the current simulated time and accepted range. Reject impossible dates, past/nonfuture instants and dates beyond 30 elapsed days. Convert once through the durable calendar mapping; handle midnight/year rollover without browser-local parsing or calendar rebasing. If approval occurs after the selected instant, retain the draft, request a new valid time and require fresh review rather than sending immediately.
- [ ] Reuse existing text limits, literal Japanese/whitespace preservation, `.TEXT`, review, editing and cancellation. Every review identifies the recipient and intended time. Only explicit review approval persists a schedule. Protect IME confirmation and queued input; exclude address/time/body entry from persistent command recall. Failed saves retain a retryable draft; committed saves consume it even if refresh/output fails.
- [ ] Persist validated pending state with stable retry identity, sender/recipient references, exact text, submission time and operational due instant. Pending inspection shows only the selected human's letters. Pending references are distinguishable from delivered-mail numbers. Do not allocate an ordinary mail number or represent submission as delivery.
- [ ] Support explicit, confirmed cancellation before due. Cancellation and release must serialize transactionally: a successful cancellation cannot later deliver or be resurrected by an uncertain submission retry. At or after due, cancellation must not falsely report success. Recipient changes or replacement of an approved schedule may use cancellation and a new composition.
- [ ] Reconcile due letters on startup/resume, mailbox refresh and the existing active-time boundary, including before relevant resident planning/context reads. Do not depend on model consent, resident frequency or AI work budgets. Reconciliation must not interrupt composition, IME input or terminal output ownership. Browser suspension may postpone processing until the next active visit; overdue delivery must not be discarded because it exceeds the AI catch-up window.
- [ ] Release each letter exactly once into ordinary local mail, atomically updating pending state and allocating its delivered-mail number. Preserve actual processing timestamps and separate intended availability metadata. Define deterministic ordering for multiple due letters. Concurrent tabs, repeated reconciliation and uncertain acknowledgements must not duplicate delivery. Storage/quota failures roll back the release and numbering together, leaving recoverable pending state.
- [ ] Before due, exclude pending subject/body from ordinary SENT/INBOX, recipient selection, pair memory, all generation prompts, reply parents and confirmation evidence. After release, catch-up visits before its availability instant must still exclude it. Preserve the existing minimum response delay relative to availability. Revalidate scheduled-parent chronology at commitment; release alone must never create read confirmation or guarantee a response. Keep scheduling IDs and queue bookkeeping out of prompts.
- [ ] Pending state and delivery metadata survive reload and versioned JSON round-trip. Validate fields, times, allowed actors, references and state transitions on direct writes/import. Legacy and deliberately empty backups remain valid without seeded schedules. Restore overdue schedules using their saved instants. Reset/restore, including identical-JSON replacement, invalidates stale drafts, cancellation approvals and reconciliation callbacks through existing world-generation safeguards.
- [ ] Preserve existing immediate single/multiple-recipient mail, Internet samples/replies, explicit-parent confirmations, calendar presentation and unrelated stored services. Scheduling causes no external mail request, mail-client handoff, model download or inference.
- [ ] Extend existing Playwright repository/controller/production coverage using controlled clocks and mocked inference. Cover time conversion in different browser timezones, exact due boundaries, expiry during composition, pending inspection/cancellation, reload/restore, late wake, duplicate retries, concurrent numbering/release/cancellation, rollback, stale-world invalidation, pre-due prompt isolation and catch-up visits on both sides of delivery. Retain functional, storage, consent, privacy, IME and terminal regressions.
- [ ] Update `docs/mail.md`, historical research, relevant README/About and storage documentation with source dates, confidence, reconstruction assumptions, limits, pending lifetime, backup/log behavior and suspended-browser semantics. Keep detailed provenance on existing documentation/About surfaces.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs focused existing mail/composition/calendar/activity/terminal coverage and `npm test -- --workers=3`; existing configuration includes TypeScript checking and production bundling. Record actual worker count, failures, corrections and unperformed checks. Review the complete diff, affected documentation links and `git diff --check`. No new framework or real-model execution is required.

## Optional validation

Native IME observation, other browser engines or a newly recovered dated PC-VAN mail manual may refine compatibility and presentation. They are not completion gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All mandatory acceptance checks are achievable before merge.
